title: openai-cc-reconciliation-delta-toolcall-recovery
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement a reconciliation compatibility layer that maps OpenAI Chat Completions (v1) request/response semantics to Redwood's internal API model with robust handling for streaming deltas, partial function_call objects, and structured output enforcement. The layer should provide deterministic mappings for roles/content, preserve finish_reason semantics, and allow safe round-tripping for customers using OpenAI-compatible SDKs while enabling Redwood optimizations (batching, caching, quantization) behind the scenes.
acceptance_criteria: Requests using OpenAI Chat Completions request shape are accepted by Redwood API and produce semantically equivalent responses for 95% of existing OpenAI-based test prompts
Streaming token deltas from Redwood are emitted in the OpenAI delta format, including incremental function_call.name/arguments where applicable
Partial/fragmented function_call objects are reconciled so that downstream SDKs receive a single coherent function_call with full arguments when stream completes
finish_reason values (stop, length, function_call, content_filter) are preserved and mapped back to OpenAI semantics
Edge cases: truncated streams can be resumed or marked with precise diagnostic metadata to aid SDK retries
Automated tests and conformance suite added (unit + integration) that validate 200+ OpenAI interoperability scenarios
implementation_notes: Introduce a RequestFingerprint computed from model, messages canonicalization (role order, trimmed whitespace), and tool_call hints to enable idempotent stream reuse and cache lookups
Build a DeltaAssembler component that consumes Redwood token deltas and emits OpenAI-style deltas. It must handle mid-stream role switches and tool_call fragment merges

Function call handling: emit incremental 'tool_call' fields consistent with OpenAI partial arguments format; buffer argument fragments server-side and only surface complete 'arguments' in the final non-delta event
Structured output: plug JSON Schema validation hooks that run on the assembled final output; on schema failure, surface structured diagnostic attachments instead of raw text
Expose lightweight diagnostics in response headers (X-Redwood-Compat-Warnings) to help debugging compatibility mismatches without breaking SDKs
Provide a compatibility-mode config flag per-route that toggles strict OpenAI mapping vs Redwood-extended behaviors (e.g., service-tool metadata enrichment)
risks: Tokenization differences between Redwood runtime and OpenAI reference may cause delta boundaries to misalign; mitigation: alignment heuristics and best-effort token anchors
Stateful buffering for function_call arguments increases memory pressure under high concurrency; mitigation: bounded buffers with backpressure and eviction policies
Overly strict structured output enforcement could break existing user prompts relying on lax parsing; mitigation: opt-in schema checks and clear error codes
Compatibility mode could hide Redwood-specific cost/latency optimizations leading to surprise billing unless documented clearly
test_plan: Unit tests for RequestFingerprint normalization (case/whitespace/message ordering)
Integration harness that runs customer OpenAI prompts through the adapter and compares tokens, finish_reason, and function_call payloads against a golden OpenAI trace
Load tests exercising buffered function_call assembly at 2x target concurrency to observe memory and latency behavior
E2E test that simulates a truncated stream and ensures clients can safely retry/resume or receive clear non-retry diagnostics
Add compatibility conformance jobs to CI that run nightly against an expanded set of prompt variations
comments: 2025-10-03 - Maya Patel: Spike completed. Verified basic mapping for role/message shapes and drafted RequestFingerprint algorithm. Found tokenization mismatch issue with gpt2-lite tokenizer used in our runtime.

2025-10-05 - Diego Morales: Implemented DeltaAssembler prototype and local integration test. Partial function_call fragments are being buffered; observed memory growth in long-running streams during load test.

2025-10-07 - Lina Becker (review): Reviewed trade-offs. Requested opt-in compatibility flag and telemetry events for deprecated edge-case mappings. Asked for clear mapping docs for finish_reason semantics.
2025-10-09 - Diego Morales: Added X-Redwood-Compat-Warnings header support and initial conformance test suite (80 scenarios). Next: harden buffering and add backpressure controls.
